guide.summary: Prototyping is easy: Composio's managed Gmail app needs no registration. Your own Google OAuth app takes about an hour to set up, but a public app that reads mail needs restricted-scope verification and a paid third-party security assessment, which takes weeks. The scopes you request decide almost everything.

composio.note: Managed OAuth is available (slug GMAIL). The Composio Gmail FAQ points to its own guide for custom Google credentials: https://composio.dev/auth/googleapps. Managed app: consent screen shows 'Composio', quota is shared, and extra scopes such as gmail.settings.basic trigger 'app is blocked'. Composio holds tokens on its servers, so Google's server-side rule for restricted scopes (security assessment) most likely applies to your app. Confirm this with Google.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes or internal tools. You need your own Google OAuth app before you put real users on it in production, or if you need scopes beyond Composio's defaults.
reasons: Your own app name and logo on the consent screen instead of 'Composio'.
Scopes beyond Composio's defaults (for example gmail.settings.basic) fail with 'app is blocked' on the managed app.
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across all Composio users.
Faster trigger polling (managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval).

scenarios.label: Prototype on Composio managed app
scenarios.when_this_applies: Building or demoing with default scopes; consent screen showing 'Composio' is acceptable.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured; no Google registration involved (c1).

waiting.basis: No provider review for the managed app.

scenarios.approval: None on your side; Composio maintains the OAuth app.

scenarios.label: Own app, Testing mode, small known group
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your own Google project with Gmail scopes (sensitive or restricted), used by up to 100 people you list, such as your team.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count, not measured; based on c6, c7, c21.

scenarios.approval: No verification. Test users see a warning screen, and authorizations and refresh tokens expire after 7 days.

scenarios.label: Public app, sensitive scopes only (gmail.send)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Production app for any Google user that uses only non-sensitive or sensitive Gmail scopes (e.g. gmail.labels, gmail.send), not restricted ones.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count: domain verification, privacy policy, justification text, demo video (c10, c22).

waiting.basis: c11 and c10; 5 business days x1.4 = 7 calendar days. Brand and sensitive reviews may overlap, so this is a rough bound.

scenarios.approval: Brand verification plus sensitive scope verification, with a demo video.

scenarios.label: Public app, restricted scopes (read/modify mail)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Production app for any Google user with gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata, gmail.settings.basic or https://mail.google.com/. Tokens held on Composio's servers and yours.

hands_on.basis: Estimate, not measured: everything in s3 plus preparing for and completing the third-party security assessment (c12, c13).

waiting.estimate: Several weeks; no exact figure documented
waiting.basis: c15 says several weeks; Google gives no exact number.

scenarios.approval: Brand verification, restricted scope verification, and an annual security assessment by a Google-approved assessor.

prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project and Google account
prerequisites.detail: You create a Google Cloud project to hold the OAuth client and consent screen, and you must enable the Gmail API in it.

prerequisites.title: Public domain with home page and privacy policy (public scenarios)
prerequisites.detail: The home page must be public and the privacy policy hosted on the same domain. The domain must be verified in Google Search Console.

prerequisites.title: Demo video (s3, s4)
prerequisites.detail: A YouTube unlisted video showing the OAuth grant and each scope's use.

prerequisites.title: Budget and assessor access (s4)
prerequisites.detail: A security assessment from a Google-approved assessor is required if restricted data goes through servers. The cost is not in the dossier.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: List the features you need and map each to the least-privilege Gmail scope. Prefer non-sensitive or sensitive scopes over restricted ones where they work, since this decides the scenario and review burden.
steps.done_when: A final scope list with a sensitivity class for each.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with managed credentials
steps.detail: Check the toolkit endpoint for composio_managed_auth_schemes, then create the auth config through Composio's API using the managed Gmail app.
steps.done_when: A connection completes with the consent screen showing Composio.

steps.title: Copy the callback URI from the Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI shown for the Gmail auth config in your Composio dashboard. Do not hard-code one. If you proxy via your domain, you will use your own endpoint instead (see the proxy step).

steps.title: Create the Google project, enable the Gmail API, configure the audience
steps.detail: Enable the Gmail API. Set user type External (or Internal for your own Workspace org). For Testing mode, add up to 100 test users. Expect 7-day token expiry and a warning screen.
steps.done_when: Project has Gmail API enabled and test users listed.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
steps.detail: Create the client as type Web application and paste the redirect URI (Composio's, or your proxy URL). Copy the client ID and secret.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and client secret.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with your client ID and secret
steps.detail: Create a custom Gmail auth config through Composio's API with your credentials and scopes, then run a test connection. Add only scopes you have declared in Google.
steps.done_when: A test user can connect and a tool call succeeds.

steps.title: Verify your domain and set up the redirect proxy
steps.detail: Google needs domains in redirect URIs verified in Search Console, and you cannot verify Composio's domain. Add a proxy endpoint on your domain that 302-redirects to Composio, and register that URL as the redirect URI. The agent can write the endpoint code.
steps.done_when: Domain is verified, listed under authorized domains, and a test login returns through your proxy.

steps.title: Draft justifications, privacy policy checklist and video script
steps.detail: Write a per-scope justification including why narrower scopes won't work, a privacy policy checklist covering Google data access, use, storage and sharing, and a demo video script.
steps.done_when: Drafts are ready for you to review and publish.

steps.title: Record the video, publish the privacy policy, verify and publish branding
steps.detail: Record the video showing the consent screen with your app name and client ID in the address bar. Run Verify Branding, then Publish branding within 7 days of a passing result.
inputs: Published home page and privacy policy

steps.title: Submit data access verification
steps.detail: Declare all scopes on the Data Access page, then submit in the Verification Center with justifications and the video link.

steps.title: Wait for Google review
steps.detail: Respond to Trust & Safety emails promptly because review pauses while Google waits for you. Restricted verification takes several weeks.

steps.title: Complete the security assessment
steps.detail: Engage a Google-approved assessor for a CASA assessment. Repeat it every 12 months.
steps.done_when: You have the Letter of Assessment and verification is granted.

traps.title: Testing mode tokens die after 7 days
traps.detail: Authorizations and refresh tokens expire after seven days unless you request only userinfo/openid scopes. Do not ship production on Testing.

traps.title: 100-user cap is lifetime and unresettable
traps.detail: Unverified apps with sensitive or restricted scopes can only add 100 new users in the project's lifetime.

traps.title: Branding must be published first, within 7 days
traps.detail: A passing brand verification expires if not published in 7 days, and you need published branding before data access review.

traps.title: Extra scopes on the managed app fail
traps.detail: Adding scopes beyond Composio's defaults gives 'app is blocked'. Use your own verified app.

traps.title: Callback domain cannot be verified by you
traps.detail: Redirect-URI domains must be in your authorized domains, so route the callback through your own domain with a 302 proxy.

traps.title: Refresh token cap per client
traps.detail: Creating more than 100 refresh tokens per account per client ID silently invalidates the oldest.

traps.title: Future quota billing
traps.detail: Standard use is free now, but exceeding quota is planned to incur charges later in 2026, with at least 90 days' notice.

blockers.symptom: 'App is blocked' or 'Google hasn't verified this app'
blockers.what_it_means: The OAuth client requests scopes Google hasn't verified for it.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove the extra scopes, or use your own OAuth app and submit those scopes for verification.
blockers.agent_can_help: Diff the requested scopes against the verified list and suggest the narrowest alternatives.

blockers.symptom: Unverified app warning on a production app
blockers.what_it_means: Sensitive or restricted scopes are requested before verification completes, and the 100-user cap applies.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft justifications and the demo video script.

blockers.symptom: Workspace user cannot authorize your app
blockers.what_it_means: Their Workspace admin controls third-party app access, or the account is in Advanced Protection.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the admin to allowlist your OAuth client ID.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the admin request with the client ID and scopes.

blockers.symptom: 'Gmail API has not been used in project'
blockers.what_it_means: The Gmail API is not enabled in your Google project.
blockers.what_to_do: Enable it under APIs & Services, wait a few minutes, and retry.

blockers.symptom: Restricted scope review requires a security assessment
blockers.what_it_means: You store or transmit restricted data on servers, which includes tokens and mail data going through Composio.
blockers.what_to_do: Book a Google-approved assessor early; or use narrower non-restricted scopes.
blockers.agent_can_help: Prepare an inventory of data flows and storage for the assessor.

open_questions: Composio's default Gmail scopes in the managed app are not stated in the dossier. Check the Composio dashboard or the toolkit endpoint.
Whether Composio storing tokens counts as 'your servers' for the CASA requirement is not confirmed. Ask Google verification support or Composio.
CASA assessor cost and duration are not in the dossier. Get quotes from approved assessors.
Real-world review timelines from developers were not found. Check developer forums.
The exact start date of Gmail API quota billing is not published; watch the Google Workspace announcements.
Specific redirect URI syntax rules were not found in the pages read. Check the Google Cloud Console error messages on client creation.
Composio's Gmail FAQ says triggers poll roughly every minute, while its managed-auth doc says a 15-minute minimum polling interval. Confirm with Composio.
Composio says Google's refresh token limit is about 50 per account, while Google's doc says 100 per account per client. Confirm which applies.
